strata.label: Early codes (Rambam, Tur and other Rishonim)
Thought, ethics, Kabbalah and other works

next_steps: Read the most relevant sources in full with get_text(ref, context=2) before relying on them.
Use get_commentary(ref) on the key Talmud or Shulchan Arukh passage to see how it was understood.
Use trace_halakha(ref) to follow a law from its source to the codes, or back.
explore_topic on a matching or related topic gives a wider overview to offer the person.
If the sources found are off-target, call again with key_terms in Hebrew/Aramaic.
Before answering, pass every citation and quote you will use to verify_citations.

trace.description:
Follow a law through the link graph: from a ref to its earlier sources (Torah, Mishnah, Talmud) and its later
codification (Rambam, Tur, Shulchan Arukh, Acharonim), split by era and date. depth 1-3.

tool_descriptions.research_question:
START HERE for any question. Finds primary sources for a question in plain language (English or Hebrew) by
meaning, by Sefaria's curated topics and by key_terms, follows the Talmud and Rambam to the Shulchan Arukh, and
returns the sources arranged by historical layer (Torah, Mishnah, Talmud, commentaries, early codes, Shulchan
Arukh and its commentaries, later codes, responsa) with short excerpts, matching topics and next steps.
key_terms: 2-4 Hebrew/Aramaic terms a scholar would use (e.g. ["כיבוד אב ואם"]); they sharpen results a lot.
Excerpts are leads: read sources in full with get_text before relying on them.
tool_descriptions.explore_topic:
A Sefaria topic (e.g. "Shabbat Candles", "Lashon Hara", "Honoring Parents", or a Hebrew name): its
description, related topics, and its curated sources arranged by historical layer with short excerpts. Use it to
give an overview of a subject or to find sources research_question missed.
tool_descriptions.get_text:
Exact text of a reference or range ("Berakhot 2a:1-5", "Mishneh Torah, Sabbath 1:1"), a named passage
("Parashat Noach 2", "Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, Vilna 7a", "Shabbat, Bameh Madlikin") or words of one segment
("Moed Katan 8b:9@29-32"). context=N adds N segments before and after, to read a passage in context. Returns
Hebrew and English per segment with the translation used for each English line, other names for the passage, a
fingerprint of the exact text and the build id. english_version picks a translation (see get_work_info).
tool_descriptions.get_commentary:
What the commentators say on a passage: excerpts from each commentary work (e.g. Rashi and Tosafot on the
Talmud, Mishnah Berurah and Magen Avraham on the Shulchan Arukh), earliest first. works narrows to specific
titles, e.g. ["Mishnah Berurah"].
tool_descriptions.verify_citations:
CALL BEFORE ANSWERING. Checks a list of citations, each {"ref": ..., "quote": optional}: the ref must exist
and the quote (Hebrew or English) must appear there, ignoring vowels, punctuation, prefix letters and -ים/-ין.
Returns all_verified, the failures, and for each match a word-exact citation (cite_as), the original words, and
the build and text fingerprint it was verified against. For a failed quote it gives the closest match and where
else the quote appears.
tool_descriptions.find_quote:
Where does this phrase come from? Finds a quotation anywhere in the corpus, earliest work first, with a
word-exact citation for each occurrence. Matching ignores vowels, punctuation, prefix letters and -ים/-ין; other
spelling variants need a second try. Dates follow traditional attributions, so check the era before calling
something the earliest source.
tool_descriptions.search:
Keyword search when you know the words: all words must appear (exact_phrase for word order). Hebrew searches
the originals, English the translations. categories e.g. ["Talmud"], ["Halakhah"]; works: exact titles.
tool_descriptions.semantic_search:
Passages by meaning only, across Tanakh, Mishnah, Tosefta, Bavli and the main codes. research_question already
uses this; call it directly for a narrower follow-up (e.g. categories=["Halakhah"]).
tool_descriptions.get_links:
All cross-references of a ref (refs only): commentaries, quotations, Ein Mishpat links to the codes.
link_types e.g. ["commentary"], ["ein mishpat / ner mitsvah"], ["quotation"].
tool_descriptions.get_work_info:
About a work: Hebrew title, author, era and date, what it comments on, available translations, sections, and
the other citation systems it can be cited by.
tool_descriptions.list_works: List works by category ("Halakhah", "Responsa", "Talmud") or part of the title, oldest first.
tool_descriptions.about_corpus:
The build this server holds: source export date, build id, code fingerprint, hashing and word-numbering rules,
counts. Cite the build id when saying a source was verified.
